subject: Capacity swap proposal + short autoscale exemption request
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: ops@hpc-consulting.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity swap proposal + short autoscale exemption request

Team —

Quick context: Nimbus Health ramped their Dedicated pool by ~40% for a timeboxed pilot; they just signaled the pilot will finish earlier than expected and want to return ~8 V100-equivalent slots next week. Product wants to reuse those slots for a short burst to run a cross-model A/B sweep tied to an enterprise launch (low tolerance for noisy preemption).

I propose a temporary 10-business-day capacity swap: move Nimbus' returned 8 slots to the "launch-sweep" pool and grant a targeted autoscale exemption (suppress preemption for that pool, max 10 days). Key asks:
- Product (Kimberly, Laura): confirm the launch schedule and whether the 10-day window is strictly required.
- Infra (Marcus, Olga): feasibility of a conditional exemption that auto-reverts after 10 days; run cost delta for 8 slots and risk notes.
- Ops vendor (cc'd): provide a quick estimate for the migration and any gating steps.

Attachments: utilization_snapshot_Q1.png (per-pool usage), temporary_autoscale_waiver_draft.docx (policy language).

Urgency: Nimbus says their return date is 2027-04-06; we'd need the swap scheduled by EOD 2027-04-05 to avoid double-booking.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity swap proposal + short autoscale exemption request

Jordan —

Thanks for the note. A few clarifying points from Product:
1) Launch-sweep timeline: hard window is 2027-04-08 to 2027-04-15 (dry run on 4/08, full sweep 4/09–4/14). We requested 10 business days to cover re-runs and a small investigation buffer; if infrastructure requires a shorter SLA we can compress to 6 business days but would like a clear rollback plan.
2) Noise sensitivity: these runs will measure latency and token-cost tradeoffs; preemption would invalidate the sweep samples and cause non-repeatability — so suppression is important.
3) Can we gate the exemption to a named pool ID and manual kill switch (no blanket cluster-wide policy)?

If infra can provide cost delta and a safe auto-revert, Product is okay moving forward. Also looping Laura for customer-facing communications (Nimbus).

-Kimberly
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ops@hpc-consulting.com
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity swap proposal + short autoscale exemption request

Team —

We can do a targeted exemption scoped to a pool tag (recommended) with an auto-revert TTL. Operational considerations and impact:
- Implementation: set poolFlag{no_preempt}=true for pool-launch-sweep; add watcher job to flip back after TTL or on explicit cancel.
- Risk: while suppressed, instances are not preemptible which increases contention risk for other pools during high demand spikes. We will not change global eviction thresholds.
- Cost: rough delta for 8 V100-e slots over 10 business days (8 * 24 * 10 = 1,920 GPU-hours). At our internal blend rate that's ~1,920 * $3.50 = $6,720. If we compress to 6 business days it's ~$4,032.
- Scheduling: we can perform the pool reassignment and flag flip in a maintenance window; migration steps are low-risk but require ops vendor to run final validations (network mounts, KV cache priming).

Next steps I propose:
1) Product confirms final window (Kimberly).
2) Finance ack on delta (Laura / accounts).
3) Ops vendor confirms validation checklist and ETA.

I'll draft the temporary exempt policy language once we lock the window.

-Marcus
From: ops@hpc-consulting.com <ops@hpc-consulting.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity swap proposal + short autoscale exemption request

Marcus / Jordan —

We can run validation and the migration on 2027-04-05 or 2027-04-06 (your choice). Checklist we will execute:
- Confirm instance images and CUDA runtime parity on destination pool
- Ensure KV cache warming for the models being swept (we need model list)
- Run preflight end-to-end smoke tests (3 samples)
- Coordinate DR fallback (if preemption occurs unexpectedly, we will failover to a warm queue and capture telemetry)

ETA and cost: 4 engineer-hours on our side for the migration + 2 hours for smoke validation = 6 billable hours at our engagement rate ($220/hr) => $1,320. If you want a standby engineer during the sweep (on-call for 6 business days) add ~$1,100/week.

Send the model list and the exact pool ID and we will confirm the migration playbook.

- HPC Ops (Sanjay)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: ops@hpc-consulting.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity swap proposal + short autoscale exemption request

Thanks everyone — quick wrap and action items:
- Product (Kimberly): finalize compressed window 2027-04-08 to 2027-04-13 (6 business days). Provide model list by Monday 2027-04-04 COB.
- Infra (Marcus): prepare the pool-flag change + auto-revert TTL for 6 business days; prepare the policy doc and cost calc (please assume conservative headroom).
- Finance/Accounts (Laura): pls ack the ~$4,032 delta to the temporary cost center; if any approval needed, flag today.
- Ops vendor (Sanjay): schedule migration for 2027-04-06 and confirm playbook once model list received.

I'll update Nimbus communications and mark the calendar. If any objections, speak up today.

Jordan
